messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER#1234 - Elevated 5xx and stream frame drops observed for streaming responses in region us-west-2. Error spike started ~03:07 UTC, p99 tail latency for streaming endpoints increased from 220ms -> 1300ms. Affected: streaming (SSE/frames) routes only. Non-streaming chunked responses appear stable. Runbook: streaming-degradation-v2.

Miguel R: I'm oncall, ack. pulling the runbook now. will triage ingress vs runtime. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre. @Ava G can you monitor infra traces?

Ava G: looking at task failures on the serving fleet, seeing repeated kv-cache eviction messages and increased GC on some quantized backends. Also seeing Nginx proxy upstream 502s for frame multiplexers. attaching quick graph: cpu spikes + queue backlog.

Linh T: getting logs from the mux layer, there's a backlog growth on stream-worker-3 and stream-worker-7. They hit connection pooling limits and upstream timeouts. suggests slow downstream processing not accept backlog.

Miguel R: decision timebox 15m for mitigations. Priority: keep customers online, reduce tail latency. Proposed steps: 1) throttle streaming endpoints in us-west-2 to 50 rps per shard, 2) shift premium customers to non-streaming chunked fallback where supported, 3) temporarily flip streaming feature-flag in control plane for affected region if throttling insufficient. Thoughts?

Priya S: Product + support here. We should avoid a blanket off if possible. If chunked fallback preserves prompt/response semantics, prefer that for customer impact. We need a short comms snippet ready in case we ask customers to switch modes.

Sam K: I can push a routing rule to shape traffic: add a dynamic rate-limit on route /v1/streams/* and route 90% of traffic for non-critical tiers to chunked fallbacks. Will prepare command.

Miguel R: execute throttle now. Sam run the rate-limit and Ava start canary checks.

Sam K: running command:
```
# apply temporary rate limit for streaming endpoints in us-west-2
redctl routing apply --region=us-west-2 --match="path:/v1/streams/*" --rate-limit=50rps --scope=region
```
Command applied at 03:15 UTC.

Ava G: canary looks better after throttle: error rate down from 6.2% -> 2.1% in 3 mins; p99 latency reduced to ~520ms. But some premium customers still see frame truncation.

Linh T: backlog draining but slowly. stream-worker-7 still sees periodic OOM-ish GC. we'll spin a replacement. scheduling a rolling drain of the two problematic workers.

Miguel R: go ahead Linh. Also toggle automatic fallback for clients that advertise streaming capability -> accept fallback if server suggests. We'll flip a gateway header that asks clients to reconnect in chunked mode.

Sam K: pushing gateway header and fallback signal:
```
# set header instructing SDKs to fallback to chunked
redctl gateway set-header --region=us-west-2 "X-Redwood-Fallback: chunked-if-supported"
```
Deployed 03:21 UTC.

support-bot: draft message for customers: "We're experiencing degraded streaming responses in us-west-2. We're throttling streaming routes and enabling fallback to non-streaming delivery. Typical client behavior is seamless; if you see truncated frames please switch to chunked mode. We'll update by 03:45 UTC."

Priya S: good start. Add note about affected time window and that Dedicated customers have been given a quota bump; include link to status page.

Miguel R: we also need to update infra: temporary quota bump for Dedicated orgs to prevent token errors when switching modes. Ava apply quota change for committed customers.

Ava G: applied quota bump for dedicated tiers in us-west-2 at 03:24 UTC. Monitoring.

Linh T: rolling drain started for stream-worker-3 and -7. New replacements spin up with updated kernel params (reduced kv-cache pressure).

Miguel R: monitoring impact window. If p99 < 600ms and error < 1% after 20m we keep throttling + fallback. If not, escalate to global streaming flag off.

Ava G: 03:29 UTC: p99 480ms, error 0.9%. backlog continues to drop. Looks stable so far. No new customer pages from support.

Sam K: adding temporary traffic shaping rules to ensure bursty clients don't overwhelm frames: token-bucket window 100 per minute with burst 200 for critical tiers; 30 per minute for free tiers.

Miguel R: logging mitigation steps in incident channel, creating post-incident playbook tasks: (a) investigation of KV eviction pattern, (b) improve backpressure in mux layer, (c) improve SDK automatic fallback behavior.

Priya S: support team drafting customer comms, ready to send 'informational' note if we see any customer-visible truncation. Keep me posted on timeline.

IncidentBot: NOTE: On-call handoff scheduled. Night oncall @Linh T will take post-mitigation watch at 03:40 UTC. Please add short summary for handoff.

Miguel R: handoff summary: throttled streaming in us-west-2 to 50rps, enabled header-based chunked fallback, drained two unhealthy stream workers, applied quota bump for Dedicated tiers, p99 reduced from 1300ms -> 480ms, error rate down to 0.9%. Continue monitoring for 1 hour and validate no regression in chunked path.

Linh T: ack, taking over for night watch. I'll keep a 30m cadence on metrics and escalate if error >1.5% or p99 >750ms.

Priya S: support ready with a one-paragraph note to send if customers DM. Template: "We saw intermittent streaming degradations in us-west-2. We've applied throttles and enabled a chunked fallback to keep requests succeeding. If you rely on frames for real-time UX please contact us and we'll prioritize mitigation for your org."

Sam K: final actions left: (1) revert temporary header after 1h if stable, (2) remove rate-limit glide after 2h, (3) document runbook gaps. I'll annotate config with run_id=2304951234.

Miguel R: good. closing active coordination. keep this thread for updates and postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
